title: Twisted-inversion GRS-duality automorphism folds the worst-line search mod an involution (forces the worst monomial direction self-dual)
evidence: The connection's two cited symmetries are both genuinely in-tree and axiom-clean: (i) dilation equivariance of the bad-scalar set (FarLineIncidenceEquivariance.explainableScalars_comp_aut / _rs_rotate), and (ii) the twisted-inversion code automorphism M(u)(x)=x^{k-1}u(1/x) that plain permutations miss (MCAMonomialEquivariance.mcaEvent_monomial; row-swap form WBPencilSymmetry.mcaEvent_swap_inv). The connection's NOVELTY claim (twisted inversion is an ignored in-tree GRS-duality automorphism) is CORRECT. What is REFUTED is the load-bearing INFERENCE in attack_plan step (c): that combining the two symmetries FORCES the worst monomial line direction (X^a,X^b) to be a FIXED POINT of the involution (a self-dual line). Two independent exact-arithmetic refutations at PROPER-subgroup primes (probe scripts/probes/_407_conn/C096_fast.py, C096_v2.py): (1) The genuine twisted involution on monomial labels is (a,b)->(k-1-a, k-1-b), NOT (-a,-b). At n=8, q=113 (mu_8 proper, index 14, inversion-closed), k=4, far-line badcount delta=3/8: TEST1 confirms badcount is EXACTLY invariant under (a,b)->(k-1-a,k-1-b) (the symmetry is real and correctly modeled), yet the involution-fixed set is EMPTY (2a==k-1==3 mod 8 has no solution), so NO direction can be self-dual while the worst direction obviously still exists -- the forcing claim is vacuously impossible. (2) Excluding the degenerate saturated band, the interior worst direction badcount=40 is attained at {(4,5),(5,4),(6,7),(7,6)}, which the genuine involution permutes as two NON-trivial 2-cycles (4,5)<->(7,6), (5,4)<->(6,7) -- distinct directions of EQUAL badcount, never a fixed point. Same pattern (12 of 16 maximizers non-self-dual) reproduced at q in {113,257,1153} (n=8) and the prize-flavored q=1009 (n=4, beta=4.99). ROOT cause: a G-invariant objective attains its max on a full G-ORBIT, not on the G-fixed-point set; symmetry never forces the maximizer to a fixed point. Additionally, dilation acts TRIVIALLY on monomial labels (x^e is a dilation eigenvector: (gx)^e = g^e x^e = scalar*x^e, same direction), so the claimed 'Z/n halves the n^2 monomial directions' contributes ZERO reduction on monomials -- only the single involution acts nontrivially, giving at most a factor-2 reduction in the NUMBER of directions to check (and only if the max were a non-fixed orbit), NOT a reduction in the per-direction circulant SPECTRAL operator dimension that is the actual prize wall.
honest_note: The connection contains a genuinely correct and useful observation (the twisted-inversion GRS-duality automorphism is in-tree, proven axiom-clean, and is a real second commuting symmetry of the bad-scalar set that no published incidence bound exploits). Only the prize-relevant CONSEQUENCE is refuted. The best one honestly gets is a factor-2 reduction in the count of monomial directions to scan (self-dual pairing), which does NOT lower the dimension of the per-frequency circulant line-incidence operator -- the BGK sqrt-cancellation / Paley eigenvalue B=max||eta_b|| for thin mu_n remains the untouched wall. The probes use small proper-subgroup primes (n=4,8; q up to 1153, plus n=4/q=1009 at beta~5); the full prize regime n=2^30, q~n^5 is out of exact-arithmetic reach, but the refuted step is a finite group-theoretic non-sequitur whose failure does not depend on scale (the fixed-point set being empty at odd k-1, and a symmetric objective maxing on orbits, are scale-independent). The saturated badcount=q band is a delta-regime degeneracy and is explicitly excluded in the decisive interior analysis. Should be logged to DISPROOF_LOG (forcing inference is a non-sequitur; dilation trivial on monomials).
wall: Welds back to BGK / Paley-graph sqrt-cancellation: after the (at most) factor-2 self-dual pairing, the residual is still the per-Z/n-frequency circulant spectral bound B=max_{b!=0}||eta_b|| (the generalized Paley eigenvalue) for thin dyadic mu_n in the n<<sqrt(q) regime -- the recognized open core, untouched by a finite involution symmetry.
